name: BootsAndVoices
source:
`` Stop treading on me'' My boots said. 
 
 God, will you please shut the fuck up for nine fucking seconds I thought as I stabbed the sentry in the neck, beginning a chain reaction of voices crying out, my own knife letting out a long surprised `` whooooaaaaa'' as it plunged into the man's cream uniform. It was his own fault I had found him out here, his pants had been expressing the discomfort of laying on the rocky ground when my squad had been coming around the corner. I wiped my knife off on the man's shoulder, my knife giving a sputter from lips that were n't real. 
 
 `` Could have given me a little warning first'' The knife said from my shoulder. 
 
 The taped ball of my dog tags agreed with a muffled groan from my chest. 
 
 `` I said no talking out on patrol, that means no talking'' I whisper to them as my squad formed up behind me. 
 
 I stopped as the wind rustled through the valley, a soft snore arising from my BDUs. At least they would sleep. I could n't wear my knee pads or the elbow pads on patrol anymore, the giggles they had were as frustrating as the dog tags. I slide my rifle around my front, it gave a long hiss out of the suppressor at the front. He was always a whiny bastard, hated me, said I always pushed his buttons. I could hear the voices from the bullets inside my magazine. 
 
 `` It's dark in here'' 
 `` It's wet in here'' 
 
 My Sergeant taps me on the arm and all at once the world gets a little quieter. The voices cut out as he turns to me. They always stop when I talk to someone, they interject when I go out alone. 
 
 `` Back on point, Lucky'' He says. 
 
 I nod my head, drawing back the charging handle of my rifle. I see the head of the cartridge poking out of the breech. 
 
 `` Hey do n't put me back in!'' It cried out. 
 
 I dropped the handle and readied the rifle. I wish I had friends. 
 
 `` That was kind of a dick move'' Said the tree I was crouched behind. 
 
 `` Fuck you'' I say as I start forward. 
 
 I wish I had more friends. My boots gurgle as I step through a muddy ditch. The tall grass whipped through the air before me in the voices of children, their voices distant and far away. Friends keep the voices back. My boots are spitting now, spitting from lips that are n't real. But friends are hard to come by in Vietnam. 
 
 `` I see the bad moon rising. I see trouble on the way'' My knife starts to sing as we advance into the jungle.
retelling:
**Perspective: The Boots**

   In the heart of a war-torn Vietnam, I found myself attached to the feet of Lucky, a soldier whose boots I would come to know intimately. Each day, we trudged through the mud and muck, the dampness seeping into my leather layers, the salt of sweat mixing with the grime.

   I could hear the rifle next to me, its metallic voice heavy with tension, echoing Lucky's anxiety. The knife clanked against his belt, sharp and unyielding, always ready for action. His dog tags jangled a melody that was more ominous than comforting. Each of them had their own voices, their own stories, and they shared them openly with the world.

   Lucky moved through the tall grass, his uniform rustling like whispers in the wind. The grass itself seemed to be filled with children's laughter, a strange and disconcerting sound in this place of death and destruction. We were all connected, part of the same tragic symphony, each note resonating with a different tone but blending together into one haunting melody.

   One day, Lucky stopped. He stood still for a moment before lifting his rifle and firing. A sentry fell to the rocky ground, a life extinguished in an instant. The silence that followed was deafening, but it didn't last long. His knife groaned, his dog tags wept, and even I felt a pang of sorrow.

   Lucky tried to silence us, but we were relentless in our chatter. We spoke of the mud underfoot, the wind rustling through the valley, and the jungle that lay ahead. He grew frustrated, trying to shut us up, but we persisted. We were more than just boots or a knife or dog tags; we were his companions, his confidants in this hellish landscape.

   The Sergeant's voice rang out, a temporary respite from our incessant chatter. But even he couldn't silence the emptiness that gnawed at Lucky's soul. We were reminders of the life he had left behind, echoes of the friends he had lost, whispers of the horror that surrounded him.

   As we moved deeper into the jungle, my steps echoed with a new rhythm. The knife began to hum an ominous tune, its notes intertwining with the rustling of leaves and the distant sounds of gunfire. We were marching towards an uncertain future, bound together by duty, sorrow, and the unyielding reality of war.

   And so, we continued our journey, Lucky and I, each step taking us further into the heart of darkness, bound by a shared history and the haunting symphony of a battlefield.
